rows.title: CT homeowners’ delinquency rates soar to one of nation’s highest during COVID pandemic
rows.standfirst: About 9.4% of the mortgages held by homeowners in the state were delinquent at the end of June.

rows.title: Lembo: CT’s economic gains could slip away soon without more federal aid
rows.standfirst: Connecticut’s recent economic gains could soon slip away without more federal aid, Comptroller Kevin P. Lembo says.

rows.title: CT’s tax receipts continue to rise despite pandemic
rows.standfirst: State income tax receipts collected since the July 15 filing deadline continue to rise, bolstering Connecticut’s rainy day fund.

rows.title: Lamont is guarding reserves for recession to come. Critics say he’s prioritizing austerity over COVID response
rows.standfirst: The governor has been withholding use of state money for pandemic relief in fear it will run out too soon.

rows.title: CT will need emergency loan soon to bolster unemployment trust
rows.standfirst: Connecticut will need an emergency federal loan soon to bolster its unemployment program, which could mean higher taxes for businesses.

rows.title: Lamont administration fines 5 more CT residents for violating COVID travel rules
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration has fined five more individuals for violating his travel restrictions and coronavirus quarantine policy.

rows.title: Lamont tells CT agencies to prep deep cost cuts for next budget
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont has directed agencies to find ways to cut spending by 10% or more in the next budget.

rows.title: COVID rental assistance program vastly oversubscribed
rows.standfirst: The funding was supposed to help 2,500 people pay rent, but 3,900 people have qualified – so far.

rows.title: Lamont’s tourism dilemma: screening for COVID could prevent spread and also hurt business
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s coronavirus quarantine policy overlooks thousands of tourists from other states to shield a damaged hospitality sector.

rows.title: Lamont extends eviction moratorium for tenants behind on rent
rows.standfirst: Extending the ban on evictions will require Lamont to declare a new public health emergency or seek legislative support.

rows.title: Low-wage workers see no relief from uncertainty of pandemic
rows.standfirst: With the $600 weekly federal unemployment boost gone, low-wage workers fear for their futures.

rows.title: Lamont applies for Trump’s new unemployment plan, but help to CT jobless will be limited
rows.standfirst: The jobless would receive half of the $600-a-week they were getting and it will take weeks to get that help.

rows.title: Breakup Eversource? Or just closely regulate?
rows.standfirst: Eversource stock fell, then rallied during a contentious hearing Monday. Its reputation with lawmakers is unlikely to rebound so easily.

rows.title: CT maxes out budget reserve as coffers approach $3.1 billion
rows.standfirst: The projections, much rosier than initially predicted, sparked renewed calls from lawmakers for more state spending to combat the pandemic.
